newsitem.title: INDONESIA: East Timorese leave Spanish embassy for Portugal.
newsitem.headline: East Timorese leave Spanish embassy for Portugal.

text.p: Four East Timorese left the Spanish embassy on Wednesday for political asylum in Portugal after entering the mission a day earlier, witnesses said.
They left the embassy in two cars of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) for Jakarta's international airport and a KLM Royal Dutch Airline flight out of the country.
The ICRC said they would go to Portugal, which has granted political asylum to 89 other East Timorese since September last year.
Diplomatic sources indentified the four as Alberto da Silva, Izidio Nogueila, Edmundo Pereira and Georgino Justino.
The Foreign Ministry in Jakarta had said it had no objection to them leaving the country.
Da Silva had been one of three East Timorese who entered the French embassy in Jakarta in an asylum bid last month. The three had been evicted from the embassy by security guards.
Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in December 1975 and incorporated it as its 27th province the following July.
The United Nations has refused to recognise Indonesian sovereignty over the territory and still regards Portugal as the administering power.
